chapter: Leaving Duke and the Goodman sextet
title: What he learned from Benny Goodman
summary: Benny and Duke were different men; Cootie learned handling and rehearsing a band, though he could not pay for rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Yeah. Did Catherine go with you when you went on the road with them?
No.
No. You maybe didn't go on the road all that much. You were probably on location quite often.
Yeah.
Yeah. Was Irving in the band?
Yeah. Irving was in the band.
Irving was in the trumpet section?
Yeah.
Irving told me one time Benny made him upset so much in the section, like he did upset people so much, that Irving says he threw his horn at the wall and smashed it up.
(Laughter)
He said it just used to break his heart.
Well, they was entirely two different men, Duke and Benny. And I learned a lot from both of them. And it was a great experience.
What all did you learn from Benny?
Well --
In the way of handling a band, you mean?
Yeah, in the way of handling the band. And -- and men, too, you know, handling the band and rehearsing the band.
Did he rehearse the band well?
Oh, yeah. Did he.
He did, huh?
Yeah.
He knew just what he wanted.
Yeah. He knew just what he wanted. The only thing that Benny did that I couldn't do was pay the men for rehearsal. I didn't have no money to pay my men for no rehearsal.
Yeah. Did he pay for rehearsal?
Yeah.
Did he?
Yeah. He'd keep the band in rehearsal for a month. Before he'd -- he'd draw them out.
Oh, I see what you mean. Yeah. Yeah. But he had everybody scared, though, Cootie.
Well --
You must have been one of the few guys in the band that was sitting up there happy. Huh?
Well, not all the time. There wasn't -- he always had to have a guy that he would pick on.
Yeah.
You know.
Yeah.
And then the other guys would be free.
(Laughter)
And some nights he would come in there, he would be gay and happy and go and play and wouldn't bother nobody. And so it would be okay, you know. It wasn't all the time that the guys would be afraid.
Oh. Yeah.
And those nights, you know, then they would play good.
Well, after all, one thing about it was the band sounded good, so the guys had to be happy.
Yeah.
It never probably sounded that good anywhere else, you know.
No.
